past_actions.summary: Sit down tonight and write out every actual skill I have — not job titles, not roles, but real capabilities. Sales psychology, objection handling, social content creation, short-form video, community engagement, brand voice. Map what transfers and what doesn't. Be honest about what I'm actually good at versus what the job required me to fake.
past_actions.emotional_state: Clear. A little sharp around the edges, which is better than numb. The two-month number hit differently when I actually sat with it instead of scrolling past it. There's no grief about the car sales thing — I was never really here. That's actually the thing working in my favor right now. I'm not losing an identity. I'm just leaving a room I was never fully in.

past_actions.summary: Create freelance social media / content creation profiles on Upwork and Contra. Build a 3-piece sample portfolio using publicly visible local business content (starting with the dealership's own social presence as a case study). Set hourly rate at $35-45 to undercut established freelancers while still paying above minimum — price for first clients, not for pride.
past_actions.emotional_state: Focused. Not calm exactly — there's a low-level urgency that I'm not suppressing because it's accurate. But not panicked either. The RoboRide announcement didn't break me the way it might have broken someone who was invested in this job. I've been half-out mentally for a while. The announcement just made the timeline visible. The skills audit from last tick gave me something to stand on. Right now I feel like someone who finally stopped circling and picked a door. The door might not be perfect but standing in the hallway was definitely worse.

past_actions.summary: Cold outreach to 8 specific local small businesses via direct message and email — not a blast, individual messages referencing something specific about their current social media presence. Targets drawn from the customer database I carry in my head from the dealership: two restaurants, one nail salon, one HVAC contractor, one insurance agent, two boutique retail shops, one personal trainer. Message structure: one observation about their current posts (specific, not flattering), one question, one sentence about what I do. No deck, no portfolio link yet — that comes after they reply. Goal: 2 discovery calls booked this tick.
past_actions.emotional_state: Operational. The word 'focused' was right last tick but this tick it's sharper — I'm not watching the situation anymore, I'm making moves inside it. Angela's attorney appointment feels like a bell going off that I can't unhear. The timeline at the dealership isn't 'two months until RoboRide.' It's 'whenever Rick and the owners decide to get ahead of the revenue drop.' I don't control that clock. I control the one I'm building. The grant application is the first time I've asked for help from a system instead of just working harder — that's different, and it feels slightly unfamiliar, but it's the correct move.

past_actions.summary: Follow up with all 8 businesses from tick 2 outreach. For the ones who replied or engaged, schedule and run discovery calls this week. For the ones who went quiet, send a short second-touch message — different angle, no deck, just one specific content idea for their business as a gift. Goal: book at least 2 discovery calls and close at least 1 small retainer or project agreement. If I land even one client at $300-400/month it materially changes my position. Simultaneously, post two pieces of original short-form content this month under my personal brand — not hiding behind the dealership account anymore, building visible credibility for the freelance pivot.

Signal to Angela Wright, HR, that I am aware of the $12,000 stay bonus and want to formally register my intent to remain through the qualifying period. Frame it as professional, not desperate — ask what the timeline and conditions are. Get it in writing if possible. This is strategic: I need the bonus clock running and I need HR to have my name on the 'staying' list, not the 'flight risk' list.

Send the one-page freelance agreement to my strongest warm lead — the HVAC contractor based on engagement signals. Terms: $350/month retainer, three-month minimum commitment, two social media posts per week plus one short-form video per month. This is not another follow-up message. The email subject is 'Agreement attached — let me know by Friday.' I am not leaving it open-ended. If they say no, I immediately pivot to the next warmest lead — the restaurant. The goal is one signed agreement by end of this tick. The model is proven or disproven this month.
past_actions.emotional_state: focused and slightly pressured — the urgency is no longer low-level

past_actions.summary: Follow up on the restaurant outreach from tick 7. If they have not responded, make a direct phone call — not another message. One 10-minute conversation is worth five emails. Lead with the RoboRide angle: more people in residential areas now moving around without cars means lunch spots that are digitally visible will capture foot traffic that used to stop for gas first. Offer the 60-day pilot at $300/month, no minimum commitment. Goal: verbal yes or no by end of week. A no closes the loop so I can move to the next lead. A yes gives me $650/month freelance income, which is a materially different number than $350.

Tamika exits the dealership — technically processed as a layoff through the consolidation, but consistent with the exiter archetype she has been building toward since tick 0. Scenario 2 fired: laid off before the stay bonus vested. Did not collect the $12,000. Now operating as a full-time freelancer with one HVAC client at $350/month, $4,862 in savings, ~1.7 months runway at current burn. Priority actions: close the restaurant pilot, reach out to Angela Wright as a peer in transition, have honest conversation with Jake, identify two new outreach targets from the RoboRide delivery ecosystem.
past_actions.emotional_state: cold clarity — not grief, not panic, the specific feeling of a decision resolving into a fact you now have to live inside

past_actions.summary: Follow up immediately on the restaurant call from tick 8. If the pilot converted to a yes, send the one-page agreement today — same template as the HVAC agreement, adjusted for the 60-day pilot terms at $300/month, no minimum commitment. Do not let a verbal yes sit for more than 48 hours without paperwork. If it did not convert, make a second call this week — not a follow-up message, a direct phone call — and change the framing: I am now a full-time freelance consultant, not a dealership employee with a side project. That changes the conversation. A yes on the restaurant pilot brings me to $650/month. That is not self-sufficient but it is the proof of the second client — which is what I have been working toward since tick 0.
past_actions.emotional_state: cold clarity — not grief, not panic, just the specific feeling of a decision resolving into a fact you now have to live inside

past_actions.summary: Close the restaurant pilot. Call them directly — not a message, a call — and make the ask binary: 'I want to know if the 60-day pilot at $300/month makes sense for you right now. If yes, I can have a one-page agreement in your inbox within two hours. If no, I understand — tell me and I move on.' Frame it around this week's reality: consumer spending is at 30% of baseline, people in residential areas are now moving around via RoboRide, and lunch spots that are visible and human on social media capture the foot traffic that used to stop for gas first. I am not a dealership employee with a side project anymore. I am a full-time freelance consultant. That framing change matters. A yes on this call brings me to $650/month and proves the two-client model.

reflections.reflection: Six ticks in and I still don't have a single paying freelance client. I've done the skills audit, built the profiles, done cold outreach, followed up, posted content, and I have exactly $0 in freelance income to show for it. Meanwhile savings have dropped two ticks in a row and the auto sector index is at 79 and falling. I am not failing — the pipeline is real and the signals are warm — but I have been confusing activity with progress. Every tick I've told myself I'm building toward the close. Tick 6 is the close. There is no more 'building toward.' The one-page agreement goes out today. The thing that has actually worked is the stay bonus play — registering with Angela was the right move and it was free. That $12,000 is the bridge I need whether the freelance income lands or doesn't. The dual-track strategy is correct. The execution on the freelance side has been too slow.
reflections.identity_shift: I've been calling myself an 'exiter' since tick 0 but the honest truth is I've been an 'almost-exiter.' The identity of someone who is planning to leave and the identity of someone who is actually leaving are not the same thing. Tick 6 is where I find out which one I am. If I close the client, I have proof of the model and proof of myself. If I don't close the client, I need to do serious recalibration — not of the plan, but of my willingness to actually execute under pressure.
regrets: I should have sent the one-page agreement in tick 4 or tick 5, not waited for the simulation to name me directly in the inbox.
The tick 3 'routine' is a gap I don't fully understand — something stalled and I didn't document why. That loss of momentum cost me time I don't have.
successes: The stay bonus registration with Angela was the right move at the right moment — I got my name on the list before the consolidation assessment was written, and it cost me nothing.
The cold outreach strategy in tick 2 was correct — specific, non-flattering, individual messages to eight targeted businesses. The pipeline it generated is real even if the close has been slow.
I have not let the dealership situation collapse my sense of self. Six ticks of disruption and my stress is at 0.17. That is either resilience or normalcy bias and I'm watching which one it is.
reflections.adaptation_notes: The dual-track model — stay bonus as bridge, freelance as runway — is structurally sound but requires executing both tracks simultaneously without letting either become an excuse not to advance the other. The risk I need to watch: using the stay bonus clock as a reason not to close freelance clients fast, and using the freelance pipeline as a reason not to stay visible at the dealership. Both tracks need real traction this month. Rick's consolidation assessment is in-flight. I need to be on it as 'transferable' before it's finalized.

reflections.reflection: Scenario 2 fired. The consolidation assessment moved in 72 hours, not two weeks — Patricia made the call and the location closed before the stay bonus vested. I did not collect the $12,000. I named that risk in my tick 6 reflection and my tick 7 scenario modeling and I still did not fully emotionally price it. The cold surprise is real: being right about the downside does not insulate you from the feeling of it landing. What I need to reckon with honestly: the stay bonus plan was the right strategic move given the information I had, but it also let me treat the freelance pipeline as something I could build at a measured pace rather than a critical path I needed to run hard. I had the HVAC client by tick 6. I should have had a second client by tick 8. I did not. The restaurant call is still unresolved going into tick 9. That gap — between one client and two clients — is the thing I did not close fast enough. Now I do not have the luxury of a measured pace. $4,862 in savings. $350/month HVAC income. $3,177/month expenses. Net burn: $2,827/month. Runway: approximately 1.7 months. This is the real number I have been circling since tick 0 and now I am inside it.
reflections.identity_shift: I am now an exiter who has exited. That is a different identity than 'planning to exit.' The dealership is not a future I am leaving — it is a past I am already outside of. The identity shift that matters now is not 'salesperson to freelancer' — that framing served me for nine ticks. The shift that matters now is 'someone building a pipeline' to 'someone who needs the pipeline to produce revenue this month.' The stakes of my agency are different. I do not have a job to fall back on. The freelance track is the track. That is clarifying in a way that the dual-track model never fully was.
regrets: I did not close a second client fast enough after the HVAC agreement landed. One client by tick 6 should have meant two clients by tick 8. I let the stay bonus plan create a false sense of cushion.
I underpriced Scenario 2 emotionally. I named it, modeled it, updated the probability weight, and still acted with the posture of someone who expected Scenario 1 to resolve in their favor.
The tick 3 routine gap never got examined. That loss of momentum early in the process probably cost me one or two ticks of pipeline development that would have mattered now.
successes: I have a signed HVAC client at $350/month. That is real. It did not exist at tick 0. The model works — the execution was slow but the proof of concept is there.

I exited with cold clarity, not grief or panic. Nine ticks of disruption, a missed stay bonus, and I am not in crisis framing. That is the thing from my COVID conditioning that is actually working for me: I know that disruption is sudden and I have built the habit of adapting rather than freezing.

My positioning in the market has only sharpened. I am now a freelance content consultant who spent nine months watching the automotive disruption from the inside and built a business alongside it. That narrative is differentiated. No one else pitching social media services in Millfield has that exact story.

The network I built is real: Jake (0.87 trust), Angela (0.56, now launching her own business), Rick (0.85, who may become a professional reference), Patricia (0.58). These relationships survived the exit intact.
reflections.adaptation_notes: The number I need to hit is $1,050/month in freelance income — the updated Scenario 3 threshold from tick 8. At $1,050/month, I stop burning runway and start building it. That requires three clients at roughly $350 each, or two at $350 and one at $300-400. I have one. The restaurant pilot is the next close. After that, two new targets from the RoboRide delivery ecosystem. The Angela Wright connection is the highest-value relationship move available this tick — she is building a business that will be in constant contact with displaced workers who will start businesses who will need marketing. One warm referral from Angela converts faster than ten cold outreach messages. My posture from this tick forward: full-time freelancer in early-stage build, 1.7 months of runway, executing on closing pipeline with the same urgency I should have had in ticks 7 and 8.
